column1: # Surface the coverage gate may not demand a check for, and why.
# One entry per line: the action name or the accessibility identifier, a TAB,
# and the reason no check can reach it.
# **An entry is a redirect, never an exemption.** It is printed on every run of
# `make e2e`, exactly as a quarantined check and a backfilled one are, because
# a list nobody is reminded of is a list that grows. A reviewer reads the
# reason; nothing here judges whether it is a good one, because nothing here
# **The bar is "no check can reach it", not "no check reaches it yet".** The
# second is ordinary work and the gate is asking for it. The first is a claim
# about the harness — a control that only exists while a menu is open, an
# action whose only effect is to end the run that would assert it — and it
# should be rare enough that a line here is worth arguing about.
# **Three kinds of entry live below, and the second is the one that does not
# meet the bar properly.** It is a redirect to a named ticket, kept here
# because the gate has to say something and a silent gap says nothing. It is
# the one to argue with first.
#   2. blocked on #254 — the browser leg has no seeded login binary
#   3. drawn only over a reply, and no fixture host ever replies
#   4. not a control — drawn text the checks READ, which no act can press
#   5. a control drawn only while a write is in flight, which the fixture never prolongs
# A `parity` step drives one action down both channels with the SAME params and
# compares the state each left. That shape cannot describe a destructive or
# creative action: the click consumes its own subject, so the dispatch that
# follows is either refused (the id is gone) or acts on something else (a new
# id). Covering these needs a parity step that can carry different params per
# channel, or compare the shape of a change rather than the state after it —
# harness work with its own argument to make, and out of 2e's scope.

column2: its parity: the click removes the binding, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same id. Dispatch and both channels' behaviour ARE covered by 2e-settings-unlink.jsonl; what no check can express is the comparison.
its parity: the click creates a binding under an id, so a dispatch with the same params collides with what the click just made. Covered by 2e-settings-doors.jsonl up to the browser leg.

its parity: the click returns the binding to its hole, and api_unbind refuses a position that holds no binding (`unbindNotABinding`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params — and a re-drag between the halves is not expressible. Both channels ARE covered by api-unbind.jsonl, each after its own drag, asserting the same hole back through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click cancels the send in flight, and api_cancel refuses a pane with nothing in flight (`nothingInFlight`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state — and a second Send between the halves is not expressible. Both channels ARE covered by api-cancel.jsonl, each after its own Send, asserting the same cancelled response through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click (or Esc) cancels the read in flight, and db_cancel refuses a pane with nothing running (`nothing is running on pane …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state — and a second slow read between the halves is not expressible inside one parity step, api_cancel's case. Both channels ARE covered: db-cancel-click.jsonl cancels one recursive-CTE read by db.<pane>.cancel and the next by dispatch, asserting the same state after each through read_pane (running false, cancelledAfterMs, the previous 2 rows kept, sort empty) and "cancelled after" in the tree; db-cancel-escape.jsonl cancels by Esc. What no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the UI half of a parity step is a click or a drag, and the operator's channel is a paste (cmd+v into the path editor), so the comparison cannot be expressed. Both channels ARE covered: the dispatch by api-paste-curl.jsonl, the paste by api-paste-curl-hotkey.jsonl, each asserting the same draft and the Filled from cURL line; what no check can express is the comparison.

display text, not a control: a static `Text` (DBPane.swift) carrying Format's refusal reason, with no press action, and the vocabulary addresses only `click`/`focus` by identifier while `expect.tree` matches by text, so no step can "press" it. Its content IS asserted: db-query-line-not-formatted.jsonl expects `not formatted: a string opened at character 39 never closes` in the tree, then its absence after the next edit.

its parity: the operator's channel is the agent's own stream — the window records a `rate_limit_event` frame from a turn on its own, with no click or drag — so the UI half of a parity step cannot be expressed: no click or drag of the operator's produces it, so there is no UI half to compare. Both channels ARE covered: the dispatch by capacity-low-reading.jsonl and capacity-passed-reset.jsonl, the stream by agent/capacity-after-turn.jsonl, each asserting the reading it lands on the indicator; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the Undo click forgets the fill it undoes, and api_undo_fill refuses a pane with nothing to undo, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state after the click — and a second fill between the halves is not expressible inside one parity step. Both channels ARE covered by api-paste-curl.jsonl, the click after one fill and the dispatch after another, each asserting the same restored draft through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click removes the database, and removing one that is gone is refused (`no database … in environment …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params. Dispatch is covered by 2e-settings-databases-dispatch.jsonl and the click by 2e-settings-databases.jsonl; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the only UI path is the `Settings…` MENU item, and a menu's buttons are not in the accessibility tree until the menu is open — the same rule that excuses every other menu control. Checks drive it by its real gesture, cmd+comma, and 2e-settings-pane.jsonl also dispatches it.

its dispatch: it needs a row id, which is minted per send and published only in read_pane — the same reason api_render_curl below is here. The operator's gesture IS covered: api-recent.jsonl presses api.recent.0.reopen and asserts the draft it rebuilds. Permanent, not blocked: nothing in the vocabulary carries a value from read_pane into a dispatch.

Two reasons, and the second is the one that lasts. A dispatch cannot hold the row id, which is minted per send and published only in read_pane; and the operator's own Copy as cURL puts its line on the PASTEBOARD, which no check can read — the act is real and its result leaves the window. `api_reopen`'s CLICK left this file when the recent strip gave it a button, because a reopen's effect lands in the draft where a check can see it; its dispatch half is still here, for the first of these reasons. Covered by WakilKitTests: curlIsPastTenseOnly, curlOnlyMentionsACredentialThereWasOne, curlEmitsAndNeverParses.

Its whole effect is a string on the SYSTEM PASTEBOARD, which no check can read — the act is real and its result leaves the window, so a check could press it and assert nothing, which is the check-that-cannot-fail this file exists to prevent rather than permit. `TerminalPane`'s own Copy is silent for the same reason and carries no indicator. The line it copies is `apiRenderCurl`'s, covered by WakilKitTests: curlIsPastTenseOnly, curlOnlyMentionsACredentialThereWasOne, curlEmitsAndNeverParses. If this pane ever draws a "copied" acknowledgement, the act becomes observable and this line should go.

its parity (3b-i; the ＋ since the compact chrome, 2026-10-26): each press opens another scratch tab, so the dispatch after the click opens a third and the two halves cannot read back the same pane (browser_new_tab's case); its other channel is ⌘T, a key and not a click or a drag. The ＋ is panes-editor-edge-to-edge.jsonl's (Untitled-2, active, typed into); ⌘T is 3b-i-editor-scratch-save.jsonl's and 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl's; the dispatch is most 3b-i-editor-* checks', each asserting the Untitled-N tab through read_pane.

its parity (3b-i): the operator's channels are ⌘W (a key) and the unsaved prompt's Don't Save, and the click consumes its own subject — the dispatch half after it would close a different tab or be refused (`the editor pane has no open tab`), api_cancel's case. Both channels ARE covered: 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl (⌘W clean, ⌘W dirty → Esc / Cancel / Don't Save) and the dispatch with and without discard in 3b-i-editor-refusals.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): there is no operator control for it — the operator moves the cursor inside Monaco, the one non-action path (design-language §11), so no UI half exists to compare. The dispatch is covered by 3b-i-editor-tabs-language.jsonl (cursor.line and cursor.column through read_pane) and refused on an empty pane in 3b-i-editor-refusals.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — the operator selects inside Monaco, the one non-action path, so no UI half exists. The dispatch is covered by most 3b-i-editor-* checks, which read selected_text back to prove what a save wrote.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — the operator's own edits are typing in Monaco, the one non-action path (`editorBufferDidChange`), so no UI half exists. The dispatch is covered by most 3b-i-editor-* checks, and its read-only refusal by 3b-i-editor-read-only.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — it runs when a window relaunches onto saved tabs, and one check is one launch. The dispatch is covered by 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl (an open, dirty tab is kept as it is); restoring after a relaunch is the runbook's row 9.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the click replaces, and the same dispatch after it finds nothing left to replace and answers a different last_replace, so the two halves cannot read back the same pane (api_cancel's case: the click consumes its own subject). Both channels ARE covered: the click (Replace All) by 3b-ii-b-replace-all.jsonl and the dispatch by 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl, each asserting last_replace's files and the Replaced … line; Replace in this file by 3b-ii-b-replace-file.jsonl, and Cancel by 3b-ii-b-replace-cancel.jsonl.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the Undo click spends the pane's one undo, and the dispatch after it is then refused (`no replace to undo`) — api_undo_fill's case. The click is 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl's (undone, restored 2, and the changed-since line for the file changed on disk), and so is the refusal of the dispatch after it.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the drag moves a tab, and the same {from, to} dispatched on the moved strip moves a different tab, so the two halves cannot read back the same order. The drag and the dispatch are each 3b-ii-b-tab-move.jsonl's, each asserting the strip's order and the active tab through read_pane.

its parity (3b-iii): the operator's channel is ↑↓ in the Changes view — keys, not a click or a drag — and the UI half of a parity step is a click or a drag only (api_fill_from_curl's case). Both channels ARE covered: the dispatch by 3b-iii-changes-drill.jsonl (across roots, both directions, clamped at the end, skipping a collapsed root, asserting the highlight and the diff tab through read_pane), the keys by 3b-iii-changes-keys.jsonl (↓ from nothing, ↑↓ across roots, after ⌘⇧G); what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-ii): the click commits what is there, and the same dispatch after it finds nothing to commit and is refused by git, so the two halves cannot read back the same state (api_cancel's case: the click consumes its own subject). Both channels ARE covered: the Commit button by 3a-ii-commit-all.jsonl and 3a-ii-identity.jsonl, ⌘⏎ in the box by 3a-ii-commit.jsonl and 3a-ii-undo.jsonl, and the dispatch by 3a-ii-commit-all.jsonl and 3a-ii-undo.jsonl, each asserting the root's rows gone or `· clean` in the tree, the message in the journal, and (3a-ii-commit, 3a-ii-identity) `git log` in a terminal; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-ii): the click undoes the last commit, and the same dispatch after it undoes the one before, or is refused on the root commit (`nothing to undo: this is the first commit`), so the two halves cannot read back the same state — api_undo_fill's case. Both channels ARE covered by 3a-ii-undo.jsonl: the ▾ menu's Undo Last Commit refills the box and puts the change back under Staged, and the dispatch after it is that refusal; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-ii): the operator's channel is the gutter peek's Stage, a button in HTML inside the WKWebView with no accessibility identifier, which the resolver cannot address (editor_peek's case). The dispatch is covered by 3a-ii-stage-change.jsonl: one of two changes staged, the other still marked, the file under Staged and Changes, and the untracked-file refusal; pressing Stage itself is walk-only (runbook row 9).

its parity (3b-iv): the operator's channel is the root's + menu (New File / New Folder), a name typed into the field and Enter or a click away — a menu, typing and a key, not one click or drag, and the UI half of a parity step is a click or a drag only (api_fill_from_curl's case). Both channels ARE covered: the + by 3b-iv-create-file.jsonl and 3b-iv-create-folder.jsonl (a pinned tab with the cursor in it, a/b and a/b/c selected, a click away committing), the dispatch by the same two (a file opened pinned, a folder shown) and its refusals (an existing name, outside the roots, a bad kind); what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3b-iv): the operator's channels are F2 and a row's context menu Rename, then typing — and neither can be driven: Orca's key table has no F-keys and no arm opens a context menu. So no UI half exists to compare, and the field's rename is walk-only (runbook rows 4–7). The dispatch is covered by 3b-iv-rename-tabs.jsonl: a folder and a file renamed under open tabs in two panes, unsaved edits and ⌘Z kept, typing across it, the open folder staying open, and its four refusals.

its parity (3b-iv): the operator's channels are ⌘⌫ with the tree focused (a key) and a row's context menu Move to Trash (no arm opens one), so no UI half of one click or drag exists. ⌘⌫ is 3b-iv-trash-key.jsonl and 3b-iv-name-refused.jsonl; the dispatch is 3b-iv-trash-selection.jsonl (selection to the next row, else the previous; a clean tab closed; its refusals) and 3b-iv-trash-tabs.jsonl (a dirty tab kept, marked deleted, not autosaved back, recreated by ⌘S).

its parity (3b-iii): the operator's channel is ⌘⏎ in a diff tab, a menu key equivalent (Maximize Pane's item, which a diff tab redirects) — a key, not a click or a drag — so no UI half can be expressed. Both channels ARE covered by 3b-iii-diff-open-file.jsonl, each opening app.txt at the diff's cursor line with the diff tab kept, and ⌘⏎ on a scratch tab maximizing; its refusal on a deleted file by 3b-iii-changes-live.jsonl.

its parity (3b-iii): the operator's channel is a click on a change mark in Monaco's gutter, inside the WKWebView — a web element with no accessibility identifier, which the resolver cannot address (editor_goto's case: inside Monaco, the one non-action path). The dispatch is covered by 3b-iii-peek.jsonl (opened on a mark, refused on an unmarked line, on an untracked file and on a diff tab in 3b-iii-diff-refusals.jsonl); the mark click is the runbook's row 8.

its parity (3b-iii): the operator's channels are ↑↓ while the peek is open (keys Monaco hands back) and the peek's ↑ ↓ buttons, which are HTML inside the WKWebView with no accessibility identifier — neither is a click on a control the resolver can address. Both the dispatch and ↑↓ ARE covered by 3b-iii-peek.jsonl, each asserting peek.index and the cursor through read_pane; the buttons are walk-only (row 8 presses ↓, a key).

its parity (3b-iii): the operator's channels are Esc in the peek (a key), typing (which closes it in the store), and the peek's × (HTML inside the WKWebView, no accessibility identifier). Esc, typing and the dispatch ARE each covered by 3b-iii-peek.jsonl, asserting peek null with the cursor and the marks kept; the × button is walk-only, in no runbook row.

its parity (2e-ii): the operator's channel is + Add a project → Open a folder (settings.projects.add.folder), which opens the macOS folder picker (NSOpenPanel) — a system panel no check can drive — so no UI half exists to compare. The dispatch is covered by 2e-ii-project-lifecycle.jsonl (a folder added, then added back whole under the name in its project.json); the picker is the runbook's rows 1, 2 and 6 (docs/wakil/phase-2e-ii-acceptance.md).

its parity (2e-ii): the operator's channel is typing in settings.project.name and leaving it — typing and a leave, not one click or drag, and the UI half of a parity step is a click or a drag only (api_fill_from_curl's case). Both channels ARE covered by 2e-ii-project-lifecycle.jsonl, the field (left by a tree click) and the dispatch, each asserting the renamed node in the tree and the old one gone; its refusals by 2e-ii-name-refusals.jsonl. What no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (2e-ii): the click removes the project, and removing one that is gone is refused, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params (db_remove_database's case). Both channels ARE covered by 2e-ii-project-lifecycle.jsonl: settings.project.remove then .confirm (the node gone, the receipt read; .keep first leaves it) and the dispatch on the project added back and renamed (the node gone).

its parity (2e-ii): a parity step compares the state each half leaves, and the two halves of this one cannot leave the same state — the tool picks the name, so whichever half runs second finds new-environment taken and creates a differently named environment, and the trees differ by construction (ctx_add_provider's case: the first half makes what the second collides with). Both channels ARE covered by 2e-ii-environment-lifecycle.jsonl: settings.tree.project.e2e-project.addEnvironment and the dispatch, each asserting environment.e2e-project.new-environment in the tree; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (2e-ii): the operator's channel is typing in settings.environment.name and leaving it — not one click or drag (ctx_rename_project's case). Both channels ARE covered: the field by 2e-ii-environment-lifecycle.jsonl (left by a tree click) and 2e-ii-rename-active-environment.jsonl (the active one, its chip following), the dispatch by 2e-ii-environment-lifecycle.jsonl, each asserting the renamed node and the old one gone; its refusals by 2e-ii-name-refusals.jsonl. What no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (2e-ii): the click removes the environment, and removing one that is gone is refused, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params (db_remove_database's case). Both channels ARE covered by 2e-ii-environment-lifecycle.jsonl: settings.environment.remove then .confirm (the node gone, the Trash receipt read; .keep first leaves it) and the dispatch on an environment made and renamed by dispatch (the node gone).

Open a folder in + Add a project (3a-iii; the tree row did this before 3a-iii): pressing it opens the macOS folder picker (NSOpenPanel), a system panel outside the app's accessibility tree that no step can choose a folder in or cancel — so a press could assert nothing but an open panel left over the run. What it adds is ctx_create_project's, dispatched with the folder as a param by 2e-ii-project-lifecycle.jsonl; the sheet around it (Cancel, Clone a repository, Back) is 3a-iii-add-project-clone.jsonl's; the picker itself is the runbook's rows 1, 2 and 6 (docs/wakil/phase-2e-ii-acceptance.md).

Change… in the clone sheet (3a-iii) opens the macOS folder picker (NSOpenPanel), the case of settings.projects.add.folder above: no step can choose a folder in it. The folder it would choose is the organisation's last clone folder by default, which 3a-iii-add-project-clone.jsonl's launch seeds (SeedSpec.CloneFolder) and asserts in the sheet; the picker is the runbook's row 9 (docs/wakil/phase-3a-iii-acceptance.md).

its parity (3a-iii): the click consumes its own subject — Clone in + Add a project clones into <folder>/<name>, and the same {url, folder} dispatched after it finds the destination there and is refused (`the destination already exists`), api_cancel's case. Both channels ARE covered by 3a-iii-add-project-clone.jsonl: the sheet's Clone (a bare repository on this Mac, pasted into the link field; the project's page opens) and the agent's dispatch (refused outside the last clone folder, on an existing destination and on a non-link, then cloning into the last folder and adding no project); what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-iii): the operator's channel is typing in a project's Agent instructions box and leaving it (or a second's pause) — typing and a leave, not one click or drag, ctx_rename_project's case. Both channels ARE covered: the boxes by 3a-iii-instructions-boxes.jsonl and agent/3a-iii-instructions-reach-agent.jsonl, the dispatch by 3a-iii-instructions-boxes.jsonl, each asserting projects[1].agent through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-iii): the click removes the account, and removing one that is gone is refused (`no git account for … in …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params (db_remove_database's case). Both channels ARE covered: Remove… → Remove in the card by 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl (Keep it first leaves it), and the dispatch and its refusal by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl.

its parity (3a-iii): Generate key generates the key and records the account on it, and the same dispatch after it is refused (`a key for … already exists: Remove or Replace the account first`) — the click consumes its own subject. Both channels ARE covered: the sheet's Generate key by 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl (the public key shown, the account recorded as ssh, ~/.ssh untouched) and the dispatch by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl (the pair under the organisation's git/ssh folder, ~/.ssh untouched); what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-iii): a parity's dispatch half must succeed, and no fixture host can answer a test — a token on a host Wakil cannot test is refused (`Wakil cannot test a token on …`), and an ssh test needs a real host that knows the key. Both channels ARE covered for that refusal: the card's Test by 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl (the note) and the dispatch by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl; a test that answers is the runbook's row 8 (docs/wakil/phase-3a-iii-acceptance.md).

its parity (3a-iii): the operator's channel is the sheet polling by itself while Sign in waits, which has no control in this build: Sign in is hidden until Wakil's OAuth apps have client ids (operator-todo.md), and a device flow needs a provider on the network either way. The dispatch is covered by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl, refused for an unknown provider (`no sign-in for e2e`), which reaches no network.

its parity (3a-iii): the operator's channel is Use your GitHub CLI login, offered only when `gh auth status` on this Mac holds a login — and a fixture gh login would be the operator's real GitHub token. The dispatch is covered by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl, refused for a login gh does not hold (`gh has no token for e2e-nobody on github.com`); the import itself is walk-only.

Copy in the SSH step (3a-iii): its whole effect is a string on the SYSTEM PASTEBOARD, which no check can read, and its "Copied" title is a button label the tree does not carry — api.recent.<…>.curl's case. What it copies is the public key the step draws, which 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl reads (`ssh-ed25519`, the key's comment); pasting it into a host is the runbook's row 8.

Open <provider>'s SSH keys page (3a-iii): pressing it opens the operator's browser at the provider's settings page — the act's whole effect leaves the window, and nothing the check could read changes. Offered only for GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket; the runbook's row 8 presses it.

Create a token on <provider> (3a-iii): pressing it opens the operator's browser at the provider's token page — the act's whole effect leaves the window (settings.org.git.account.add.openKeys' case). The token step it sits in is 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl's (Bitbucket's username, a pasted token, Connect).
Open <host> in Sign in (3a-iii): drawn only while a device code is shown, and Sign in has no control in this build (ctx_git_device_poll's case); its effect would leave the window besides.
the GitHub CLI login choice (3a-iii): drawn only when `gh auth status` on this Mac holds a login, which a fixture could hold only with the operator's real token (ctx_git_gh_import's case).

its parity (3a-iii): Sign in has no control in this build — it is hidden until Wakil's OAuth apps have client ids (operator-todo.md), and a device flow needs a provider on the network either way, so no UI half exists. The dispatch is covered by 3a-iii-git-account-actions.jsonl, refused without a client id (`Sign in is not set up for github in this build; use an SSH key or a token`), which reaches no network; Sign in is walk-only.

its parity (3a-iv): the click (the in-place field's Stash, or Return in it) stashes the root's changes, and the same dispatch after it finds nothing to stash and is refused (`No local changes to stash`), so the two halves cannot read back the same state — editor_changes_commit's case. Both channels ARE covered: ▾ → Stash → Stash, Stash Including Untracked and Stash Staged by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl (the rows gone from the tree, `git stash list` and the stash's untracked parent read in a terminal), the dispatch in each mode there and by 3a-iv-stash-by-id.jsonl, and the refusal; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-iv): the click (a stash row's Apply) puts the stash's changes back, and the same {index, id} dispatched after it lands on a tree that already holds them, which git refuses or clashes on, so the two halves cannot read back the same state. The dispatch is covered by 3a-iv-stash-by-id.jsonl (the changes back, the stash kept, and the moved-list refusal `The stash list changed; look again`), ▾ → Stash → Apply Latest Stash by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl; the row's Apply by 3a-iv-stash-rows.jsonl (on a clean tree: the changes back, the stash kept).

its parity (3a-iv): the click (a stash row's Pop) applies the stash and drops it, and the same {index, id} dispatched after it is refused (`The stash list changed; look again`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params — the click consumes its own subject. The dispatch is covered by 3a-iv-stash-by-id.jsonl (a pop by a moved position refused, then by its new position), ▾ → Stash → Pop Latest Stash by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-iv, Decision 46): from the agent's channel it is priced gate, so a dispatch parks for the operator's confirmation (`delete branch X in <root>`) and the request is held open until someone answers — an agent's proposal has no timeout (MCPServer.parkForConfirmation, R1). A check's dispatch holds its step for that whole time and no later step can run to answer the plane, so the dispatch can never be asserted (measured: the tools/call blocks until the harness's own reply deadline). The scripted agent (agent/) could ask instead, but its params are fixed in e2e/stub/script.json and cannot name the per-run fixture root an absolute `root` needs. The pane's channel IS covered: 3a-iv-branch-menu.jsonl deletes an unmerged and a merged branch through Delete Branch… with Keep it and Delete; the agent's plane is the runbook's row 10.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-iv, Decision 46): priced gate for the agent, so a dispatch parks (`drop stash <id7> in <root>`) and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The pane's channel IS covered: 3a-iv-stash-rows.jsonl presses a row's Drop, Keep it, then Drop, and asserts the row gone and `git stash list` one shorter.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-iv, Decision 46): priced gate for the agent, so a dispatch parks (`drop N stashes in <root>`) and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The pane's channel IS covered: 3a-iv-stash-rows.jsonl presses Drop All…, Keep it, then Drop, and asserts the list empty.

the context line's Branch segment (3a-iv): drawn only while the line is promoted, which is while the pointer hovers it, and no step kind hovers — the resting line is one element whose text the checks read. Its reading IS asserted at rest, `STAGING e2e-portal: main`, then `: topic` after a switch, by 3a-iv-switch-branch-palette.jsonl; the picker it opens is the one the Changes header opens, pressed by 3a-iv-branch-picker.jsonl. Opening it from the line is the runbook's rows 1–2.

the branch picker's root tabs (3a-iv): drawn only in the context line's picker (a Changes header's picker is for its one root), and that picker opens only from the hovered Branch segment — window.contextLine.branch's case. Switching roots is the runbook's.

▾ → Branch → Create Branch… (3a-iv): an item of a submenu, which the accessibility tree the resolver reads does not hold (measured: pressing the Branch item leaves `menu item (selected) Branch` and no child menu), so no click can name it. It is reached by keys instead — the submenu opened with Right, Return on its first item — by 3a-iv-branch-menu.jsonl, which asserts the field it opens (focused, `New branch name`) and the branch it creates.

▾ → Branch → Rename Branch… (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-branch-menu.jsonl, which asserts the field (`New name for the branch`, holding the current name) and the rename, by the field's button and by dispatch (parity).

▾ → Branch → Delete Branch… (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-branch-menu.jsonl, which asserts the picker it opens (`Choose the branch to delete`), the in-place confirmation and both deletes.

▾ → Stash → Stash (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl, which asserts the field (focused, `Message (optional)`, kept with its text when focus leaves, closed by Escape) and the stash Return makes.

▾ → Stash → Stash Including Untracked (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl, which asserts e2e-api clean, untracked files included, and one stash in `git stash list`.

▾ → Stash → Stash Staged (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl, which asserts the staged file gone, the untracked one kept, and `On main: staged only` in `git stash list`.
▾ → Stash → Pop Latest Stash (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl, which asserts the change back and the stash list empty.
▾ → Stash → Apply Latest Stash (3a-iv): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys by 3a-iv-stash-menu.jsonl, which asserts the changes back and the stash kept.

its parity (3a-v-b): the click (a picker row in Merge Branch…) merges and stops on the conflicts, and the same dispatch after it is refused (`A merge is in progress in <root>; finish or abort it first`), so the two halves cannot read back the same state (editor_changes_commit's case: the click consumes its own subject). Both channels ARE covered by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl: the picker row (`Merge stopped on conflicts in doc, gone; resolve them below`, `merging feature`, the two rows) and the dispatch after an Abort (`merging feature` again), plus the in-progress refusal.

its parity (3a-v-b): the click (a picker row in Rebase Branch…) rebases and stops at step 1, and the same dispatch after it is refused (`A rebase is in progress in`), editor_changes_merge's case. Both channels ARE covered by 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl: the picker row (`Rebase stopped on conflicts in doc (step 1 of 3)`, `rebasing 1/3 onto main`) and the dispatch after an Abort, plus the in-progress refusal.

its parity (3a-v-b): the click (Commit Merge / Continue Rebase) finishes the operation or moves the rebase to its next stop, and the same dispatch after it is refused (`Nothing to continue`, or `Resolve the conflicts in notes first` at the next stop), so the two halves cannot read back the same state (editor_changes_commit's case). Both channels ARE covered: the clicks by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl (`git log` reads `Merge branch 'feature'` with two parents) and 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl (`rebasing 3/3 onto main`), the dispatch's three refusals by both.

its parity (3a-v-b): the operator's channel is Keep File in a delete/modify row's context menu, and no arm opens a context menu (editor_rename's case), so no UI half of one click exists. The dispatch is covered by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl: `gone, deleted by them` leaves Merge Changes, the reason drops to `Resolve 1 conflict first`, and after the merge `gone` still reads `old, mine`. The menu is the runbook's row 10's file and walk-only.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-v-b, R1): priced gate for the agent, so a dispatch parks (`take the incoming <path> whole in <root>; edits made to it are lost`) and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. And the pane's channel is Accept All Current / Accept All Incoming / Delete File in a conflicted row's context menu, which no arm opens (editor_rename's case). So neither channel can be driven by a check; it is the runbook's rows 5 (the menu and its in-place confirm) and 10 (the agent's plane), and its Go half is pinned by gitresolve_test.go.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-v-b, Decision 46): priced gate for the agent, so a dispatch parks (`abort the <kind> in <root>`) and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The pane's channel IS covered: 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl presses ▾ → Abort Merge, Keep it (nothing changes), then Abort (`· clean`, no MERGE_HEAD); 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl the same for Abort Rebase.

its dispatch and its parity (3a-v-b, Decision 46): priced gate for the agent, so a dispatch parks and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The pane's channel IS covered by 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl: ▾ → Skip Commit, `"rework 1"? Its changes are left out of the rebase.`, Keep it (still `rebasing 1/3`), then at step 3 Skip (`· clean`, `git log main..rework` reads `add readme|rework 1`).

its dispatch and its parity (3a-v-b, call 13): priced gate for the agent, and gated before it is refused, so even a dispatch with no clash parks and holds its step open until the operator answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The pane's channel IS covered: 3a-iv-branch-blocked.jsonl presses Undo Apply and Undo after Bring Them Along (`· clean`, `theirs`, the stash kept); 3a-v-b-stash-clash.jsonl presses Keep it and then Undo over an edited file (`index.txt changed since the clash; Undo Apply would lose that — resolve it by hand`, the edit and the stash kept).

its parity (3a-v-b, R3): the operator's channel is Accept Current / Incoming / Both Change in the actions row over a block, an overlay widget in HTML inside the WKWebView with no accessibility identifier, which the resolver cannot address (editor_peek's case). The dispatch is covered by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl (both: `top|main|feature|bottom` on disk after editor_save; refused on the Compare tab and on a stale line) and 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl (incoming); the row is the runbook's rows 3–6.

its parity (3a-v-b): the operator's channel is Compare Changes in the same in-page actions row, editor_conflict_accept's case. The dispatch is covered by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl: a second tab with diff.conflict true and the title `doc (Current ↔ Incoming)`; the row's press is the runbook's row 3.

▾ → Branch → Merge Branch… (3a-v-b): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys (Right, Return) by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl, which asserts the picker it opens (`Choose the branch to merge in`, its filter focused, Escape closing it) and the merge it starts.

▾ → Branch → Rebase Branch… (3a-v-b): a submenu item, editor.changes.<…>.branch.create's case. Reached by keys (Right, Down, Return) by 3a-v-b-rebase.jsonl, which asserts the picker it opens (`Choose the branch to rebase onto`, its filter focused) and the rebase it starts.

Accept All Current in a conflicted row's context menu (3a-v-b): no arm opens a context menu (editor_rename's case), so no click can name it. editor_changes_take's dispatch is gated as well, so neither channel is driven; walk-only, the runbook's row 5.
Accept All Incoming in a conflicted row's context menu (3a-v-b): editor.changes.row:<…>/<…>:conflicts.takeCurrent's case; walk-only, the runbook's row 5.
Delete File in a delete/modify row's context menu (3a-v-b): editor.changes.row:<…>/<…>:conflicts.takeCurrent's case; walk-only.
Keep File in a delete/modify row's context menu (3a-v-b): no arm opens a context menu. What it runs, editor_changes_keep_file, is dispatched by 3a-v-b-merge.jsonl; the menu is walk-only.

the whole-file take's Keep it (3a-v-b, Rule 1): drawn only after a choice in a conflicted row's context menu, which no arm opens, and the agent's take parks rather than asking in place — so nothing a check can do ever draws it. The same ChangesConfirm's Keep it is pressed under Abort, Skip and Undo Apply by 3a-v-b-merge, 3a-v-b-rebase and 3a-v-b-stash-clash; this one is the runbook's row 5.
the whole-file take's Accept / Delete (3a-v-b, Rule 1): editor.changes.row:<…>/<…>:conflicts.take.keep's case — drawn only after a context-menu choice; walk-only, the runbook's row 5.

its parity (connections): the click creates a connection, a catalog kind under a name Go picks and Custom server under the typed one, so the same params dispatched after it add a second one (atlassian-2) or are refused (`already has a connection named`). That is ctx_add_provider's case. Both channels ARE covered: the clicks by connections-settings-list.jsonl (Atlassian (Confluence)) and connections-allow-agent.jsonl (Custom server), the dispatch by connections-allow-secrets-parity.jsonl, connections-rename-remove.jsonl and connections-browser-signout-parity.jsonl, each asserting the connection's row or page. What no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (connections): the operator's channel is typing in a field of the connection's page and leaving it, not one click or drag (api_update_entry's case). The hints a Check records are a side effect of listing, not a control. Both channels ARE covered by connections-rename-remove.jsonl: a rename typed into <name>.name and left with Return, asserted by the page following the new name and the journal, and a dispatch renaming another connection and changing its command, asserted on its page. connections-allow-secrets-parity.jsonl dispatches its hints and reads the rows they draw.

its parity (connections): the click removes the connection, and removing one that is gone is refused (`no connection … in …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params (db_remove_database's case). Both channels ARE covered by connections-rename-remove.jsonl: <name>.remove pressed, the list without it, and the dispatch on another connection, the list re-read without it and a second dispatch refused.

its parity (3c-i): the operator's channel is the address field — typing and Return, keys and not a click or a drag (api_fill_from_curl's case). Both channels ARE covered: typing by 3c-i-open-and-navigate.jsonl (Page A, then ⌘L and Page B), the dispatch by 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl and 3c-i-tabs.jsonl, each reading the url and title back.

its parity (3c-i): each press opens another tab, so the dispatch after the click opens a third and the two halves cannot read back the same pane (editor_new_scratch's case). The ＋ click and ⌘T are 3c-i-new-tab-entry.jsonl's and 3c-i-tabs.jsonl's; the dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's and 3c-i-narrow.jsonl's, each reading the new tab's id and selection back.

its parity (3c-i): no operator control opens a URL in the browser from outside the pane — that arrives with 3c-iii's links from the terminal and editor — so no UI half exists. The dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's and 3c-i-settings.jsonl's: it opens the pane and reads Page A's title back.

its parity (3c-i): every reload is another load, and the fixture pages are the same after each, so nothing read_pane or the tree carries differs before and after the click — the parity would refuse it as having changed nothing. The click is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's (journal, title) and Try Again's 3c-i-load-error.jsonl's; the dispatch re-runs the page's own prompt in 3c-i-prompt.jsonl.

its parity (3c-i): the operator's channel is ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0, keys and not a click or a drag (editor_new_scratch's case); the pane draws no zoom control. The keys are 3c-i-zoom.jsonl's (1.1, 1.25, per host, reset); the dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's (in, reset).

its parity (3c-i): the click consumes its own subject — the dispatch after it closes another tab or is refused (`the browser pane has no tab …`), editor_close's case — and the tab's × is drawn only under the pointer (browser.tab.<…>.close). ⌘W is 3c-i-tabs.jsonl's; the dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's.

its parity (3c-i): the operator's channels are ⌘⇧T and the Reopen Closed Tab menu item — a key and a menu, not a click or a drag — and each reopen consumes the closed stack, so the halves could not agree anyway. ⌘⇧T is 3c-i-tabs.jsonl's; the dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's (t3, b.html).

its parity (3c-i): the operator's channel is ⌘F and typing into the find field — keys, not a click or a drag. The keys are 3c-i-find.jsonl's (needle, 1 of 3); the dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's, reading the query and count back.

its parity (3c-i): each Next or Previous moves the match, so the dispatch after the click lands one further and the halves cannot read back the same count (editor_replace's case). The clicks and ⌘G are 3c-i-find.jsonl's; the dispatch, both ways and refused once the bar is closed, is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's.

its parity (3c-i): what it changes is where the keyboard is — view focus, not pane state — and neither read_pane nor the tree text a parity compares carries it; focus is an expect, not a state read. ⌘L is 3c-i-keys-reach-wakil.jsonl's and the dispatch 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's, each followed by expect.focus browser.address.

its parity (3c-i): no operator control — the window runs it when it reopens a saved layout, and one check is one launch (editor_restore's case). The dispatch is 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl's (the saved tabs and their ids kept); a relaunch is the runbook's row 4.

its parity (3c-i): before the click a running download's bytes change every tick, so the state a parity reads first never settles; and a dispatch after the click finds the download already ended and changes nothing (api_cancel's case). The click is 3c-i-download.jsonl's on d1, the dispatch the same check's on d2, each reading cancelled back; a real download's Cancel is the runbook's row 7.

its dispatch and its parity (3c-i, Decision 48): priced gate in every environment, so a dispatch parks for the operator's confirmation and holds its step open until someone answers — editor_changes_branch_delete's case. The operator's channel IS covered: 3c-i-settings.jsonl asks, keeps, asks again, deletes and reads `Deleted E2E Fixture's browsing data.` and the journal; the refusal for another organisation is WakilKit's (clearDataRefusesWhenTheOrganisationTheQuestionNamedIsNotActive).

a tab's × (3c-i): drawn only while the pointer is over the tab, and no step kind moves the pointer without clicking — a click on the tab selects it instead. Closing is ⌘W in 3c-i-tabs.jsonl and browser_close_tab in 3c-i-agent-drives.jsonl; the × itself is walk-only.

column1: # Every one of these needs a real browser trip and a real one-year credential at
# Anthropic. A check that reached them would mint a credential on every run,
# which is a side effect no gate is worth. #254 is the ticket for a seeded login
# binary on the provider record; these become ordinary work the day it lands.
# #254 was PARKED on 2026-09-26 (docs/wakil/parked.md), not done — closed with
# the tracker's move to a bug inbox — so every line below still stands. #325
# (Adopt and Register vanish under a sign-in error banner) is walk-only for the
# same reason: the banner is drawn only by a trip that started, and the one
# made-up claude path that fails safely today would be a real browser trip if

column2: #254. Opens a browser on the operator's machine and authenticates as them. No harness can drive it and none should: every run would leave a real credential behind.
#254. The control that does the above.
#254. Goes straight to the browser by design — no confirmation step — so pressing it IS starting a real trip.
#254. Starts a fresh trip, and only appears when the config dir is already signed in, which itself needs a real credential.
#254. Only exists while a browser trip is in flight.
#254. Only exists while waiting on a live mint.
#254. Drawn only by the states a finished trip reaches — added, refused, cancelled, timedOut, uncertain, failed.

column1: # The fixture's entries resolve to `.invalid` hosts on purpose, and the one live
# listener (`slow`) never answers; wakil-http refuses a cleartext origin, so no
# fixture server can answer either. A control drawn only over a reply cannot be
# reached by any check. The runbook's check 5 walks it against a real API.

column2: the Body · Headers choice (W20) is drawn only over a reply, and no fixture host ever replies — every entry is `.invalid` or the never-answering `slow`, and wakil-http refuses http://. apiResponseOffersHeaders and apiResponseHeaderRows are pinned in ApiPaneLayoutTests; the drawn table is the runbook's check 5.

its parity (connections): a start succeeds only over a sign-in server's reply (its resource and authorization-server metadata and a client registration), and no fixture host answers one; and the UI half of a start that succeeds opens the operator's own browser on the page it answers. What both channels do without a reply IS covered by connections-browser-signout-parity.jsonl: Sign in with … pressed and the dispatch, each refused with the same sentence (`could not read portal's sign-in details`) against a closed loopback port, so nothing leaves the machine.

its parity (connections): a wait ends only when the browser comes back to the loopback callback with the code and state a successful start minted, so its UI half needs the start above, and no step can carry that state into a request. Its dispatch with no start in flight is covered by connections-browser-signout-parity.jsonl (refused: `no sign-in to portal is in progress`).

column1: # ---- 4. Not a control: drawn text the checks read ----------------------------
# 2d-ii put identifiers on views that draw text and take no input. The gate
# counts an identifier covered only when a check clicks, focuses, types into or
# drags it, and none of those acts applies to a static text or a container: an
# AXPress on one is refused (action unsupported) and AXFocused is not settable.
# What each says IS asserted, through `expect.tree`, in the checks named — the
# vocabulary just has no way to credit a read to an identifier. If a read ever
# counts as coverage, every line here should go.

column2: the composer bar's container (.contain), which holds the field, the heard text and the hint and takes no input itself. Its contents are read by every 2d-ii voice check; the field inside it is `window.composer`, which they type into.

a Text: the words heard while ⌥ is held, or the notice that replaces them. Read, not pressed — 2d-ii-voice-silence.jsonl asserts "Hearing nothing from E2E Microphone" and the words that clear it; 2d-ii-voice-lands-unsent.jsonl and 2d-ii-voice-escape.jsonl assert the words mid-hold.

a Text: the bar's hint. Read, not pressed — the keys hint ("TO SPEAK"), the listening hint ("RELEASE TO PUT IT IN THE LINE") and the landed hint ("HEARD · RETURN SENDS · EDIT FIRST") are asserted by the 2d-ii voice checks.

the thought thread's container (.contain), which takes hits only on its rows and the "earlier" line. Its rows are pressed by 2d-ii-thread-earlier.jsonl as window.thread.row.<id> and window.thread.earlier.

a Text: the Speech row's "unknown engine 'x', using Apple". Read, not pressed — 2d-ii-settings-speech.jsonl asserts it after a dispatched unknown id and a reload, and its absence after Apple is chosen.

the palette's container (.contain, palette rework): it holds the header, the query line, the rows and the footer, and takes no input itself — the dimmer around it takes the dismissing click. Its contents are read by every palette-*.jsonl check ("OPEN OR SWITCH TO", "RUN A COMMAND", the "N of M" count); the field inside it is palette.query, typed into, and its rows are palette.row.<id>, pressed.

a Text (palette rework): an input step's title, uppercased, where the mode's name was. Read, not pressed — palette-command-step.jsonl and palette-escape.jsonl assert "PANE KIND", palette-run-error.jsonl "CURL COMMAND", palette-switch-environment.jsonl "ENVIRONMENT", palette-table-row.jsonl a drill's "BOOKINGS"; palette-escape.jsonl asserts it gone after one Esc.

a Text (palette rework, rule 8): a run's error, drawn whole under the query line. Display text with no press action. Read, not pressed — palette-run-error.jsonl asserts "no entry in staging has that host" with the step and the typed line still there.

the Settings capacity strip's scroll container (provider capacity), which takes no input. Its rows are read by capacity-low-reading.jsonl and capacity-passed-reset.jsonl, beside the accounts table's own CREDENTIAL and SIGN-IN headers.

the capacity indicator beside ACCOUNT (provider capacity): it has no press action, and it refuses AXFocused (measured 2026-10-10: axresolve not_focusable), because `.focusable(interactions: .activate)` keeps a click from taking the composer's focus (Rule 6) and joins the key loop only with macOS Keyboard navigation on. Its card opens on hover or on that focus, and the vocabulary has no hover step, so opening the card is walk-only. What it draws is read by capacity-at-launch.jsonl (the launch probe, no turn), capacity-low-reading.jsonl, capacity-passed-reset.jsonl and agent/capacity-after-turn.jsonl.

the Monaco host's container (3b-i): an NSViewRepresentable holding the WKWebView, with no press action of its own. Typing into it is driven by keys: 3b-i-editor-scratch-save.jsonl types after ⌘T and after a save, and asserts the text through read_pane.
a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): a tab's notice, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-read-only.jsonl asserts "ro.bin is a binary file" in the tree and through read_pane.

the disk line's container (.contain, 3b-i): its text and two buttons. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl asserts "disk.txt changed on disk" and its absence while comparing and after Reload; its buttons are editor.reload and editor.compare, pressed.

Compare's Monaco host (3b-i): a WKWebView container with no press action. 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl asserts Compare's header opens and closes (button and Esc); what the diff shows is the operator's ruling (runbook row 6).

a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): drawn only when the file cannot be read back for Compare. The fixture's files are always readable and no step can make one unreadable mid-launch; display text with no press action either way. The runbook walks Compare.

a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): the path field's failure, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-save-as-field.jsonl asserts "is outside the active project's roots; editor reads and writes are confined to them (Invariant 6, Decision 36)" with the typed path still in the field.

the empty pane's hint (3b-i, .combine): "⌘P to open a file · ⌘T for a scratch tab", with no press action. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl asserts it after the last tab closes, and its absence after ⌘W closes the pane.

the unsaved prompt's container (.contain, 3b-i): the message and three buttons. Read, not pressed — every prompt check asserts its message; its buttons editor.unsaved.save / .dontSave / .cancel are pressed by 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl, 3b-i-editor-unsaved-save.jsonl and 3b-i-editor-unsaved-org-switch.jsonl.

a Text (3b-i): the prompt's question. Read, not pressed — "Save changes to Untitled-2?" (3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl), "Save changes to kept.txt?" (3b-i-editor-unsaved-save.jsonl), "Unsaved changes in Untitled-1" (3b-i-editor-unsaved-org-switch.jsonl, 3b-i-editor-unsaved-quit.jsonl).

the saving tick (3b-i, Rule 5): a 2 pt shape drawn only while a write is in flight, which against the fixture's tiny files lasts milliseconds — never long enough for a tree read to see. `saving` is asserted false after each save through read_pane; seeing the tick is the runbook's walk.

the row detail strip's container (.contain, RowDetailStrip.swift): its labels and values, with no press action of its own. What it draws is read by db-detail-strip.jsonl and db-detail-big-cells.jsonl; its values are db.<pane>.detail.<i>, read.

a Text (db pane footer): the flight line, "running …" while a read is in flight and "cancelled after …" once one is cancelled. Read, not pressed — db-cancel-click.jsonl and db-cancel-escape.jsonl assert "cancelled after" in the tree, and db-cancel-click.jsonl its absence after the next read.

the db grid's surface (.contain): it has no press action and refuses AXFocused (measured: axresolve not_focusable), as a focusable SwiftUI surface with no AX focus attribute — its keyboard focus is SwiftUI's own, given when the pane is focused, which the checks do by clicking rail.db-<n>. Its keys are driven that way: ↑↓, Space and Esc by db-detail-strip.jsonl, ⌘C by db-grid-copy.jsonl; its rows' contents are read through read_pane.

the row's ⓘ: drawn only while the pointer hovers inside a row whose children are ignored by accessibility (.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)), so it is never in the tree, and the vocabulary has no hover step (window.capacity's case). The same toggle is the row's "Show details" accessibility action and Space on the grid, and db-detail-strip.jsonl drives Space (open, close, another row). Pressing the ⓘ itself is walk-only.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): settings.json's read or parse error, drawn only when ~/.wakil/settings.json cannot be read. The seed never writes that file, and no step can write it mid-launch — editor writes are confined to the active project's roots (Invariant 6, Decision 36) and ~/.wakil is outside them; display text with no press action either way. Its wording and the defaults it leaves in force are pinned by internal/wakilcore/editorsettings_test.go and WakilKitTests EditorSettingsTests; the runbook walks it with a hand-broken file.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses a word-wrap write the pane itself offers (On or Off), and Go refuses a boolean only when settings.json does not parse — which, as for settings.editor.error, no fixture or step can produce. Display text with no press action. 3b-v-editor-settings-nodes.jsonl drives both choices and asserts each write on disk.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses an autosave mode the pane offers (off, pause, focus are each valid), which happens only over a settings.json that does not parse — no fixture or step can produce one (settings.editor.error's reason). Display text with no press action. 3b-v-editor-settings-nodes.jsonl drives all three modes and asserts each on disk.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses Spaces or Tabs, which it does only for a project.json filed under another organisation or unreadable — and either one drops the project from the settings tree, so its Editor node draws `gone` instead of this form and the refusal has nowhere to appear. Display text with no press action. 3b-v-project-editor-settings.jsonl drives both choices (Tabs through parity) and asserts each on disk.

the editor's left column's container (.contain, 3b-ii): its header, the tree or the search view, and the edge, and it takes no input itself. What it draws is read by every 3b-ii-* check; its controls are editor.column.files / .search, pressed by 3b-ii-tree-toggle.jsonl, editor.column.edge, dragged there, and the tree's and search's own.

the tree's load tick (3b-ii, Rule 5): a shape drawn only while a root lists or a heavy folder loads, which against the fixture's small roots lasts milliseconds — never long enough for a tree read to see. 3b-ii-tree-ignored-heavy.jsonl asserts what the load brings (autoload.php under vendor); seeing the tick is the runbook's walk.

a Text (3b-ii, Rule 8): a root's or a heavy folder's listing error, drawn whole under its row. Every fixture root lists and vendor loads, and no step can make one unreadable mid-launch; display text with no press action either way. column1: # ---- 5. A control that exists only while a write is in flight ----------------
# Settings' login Cancel is the precedent (section 2), for a different reason:
# here the wait is real but too short for any act to land on.

column2: the saving tick's Cancel (3b-i, Rule 4): a control that exists only while a write is in flight, which against the fixture lasts milliseconds — a press cannot land on it, and wakil-files writes through a temp file and a rename, so no fixture path can make a write wait. Cancelling a save is the runbook's walk.

its parity (3a-ii-b): the click stages the selected lines, and the same dispatch after it finds them already staged and is refused (`the selection holds no change`), so the two halves cannot read back the same state — editor_changes_commit's case. Both channels ARE covered by 3a-ii-b-ranges.jsonl: the dispatch stages line 3 of app.txt and the header button (editor.diff.stageRanges) stages README.md's changed line, each asserted with `git diff --cached --numstat` in a terminal, and the no-change refusal; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (3a-ii-b): the click unstages the selected lines, and the same dispatch after it finds nothing staged there and is refused (`the selection holds no change`), so the two halves cannot read back the same state — editor_changes_commit's case. Both channels ARE covered by 3a-ii-b-ranges.jsonl: the header button (editor.diff.unstageRanges) unstages README.md's line and the dispatch unstages app.txt's added line while keeping its changed one staged, each asserted with `git diff` in a terminal; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity (2e-iii): the operator's channel is typing in a field of the entry's section and leaving it — not one click or drag (ctx_rename_project's case); Clear token is a click but sends only clearToken, a part of the action. Both channels ARE covered by 2e-iii-api-entries.jsonl: the base URL and the name left by a tree click, Clear token pressed, and the dispatch renaming an entry, changing its URL, and refused on authHeader Host.

its parity (2e-iii): the click removes the entry, and removing one that is gone is refused, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params (db_remove_database's case). Both channels ARE covered by 2e-iii-api-entries.jsonl: settings.api.<name>.remove then .confirm (the entry gone; .keep first leaves it) and the dispatch on an entry added for it.

the card's Cancel while a Test runs (3a-iii, Rule 4): a control that exists only while a Test is in flight, and every Test the fixture can make ends at once — a token on a host Wakil cannot test is refused before any network, and an ssh account's host does not resolve. Holding a Test open would need an ssh host that accepts and never answers, which the fixture does not serve. The Test itself is 3a-iii-git-accounts.jsonl's; a slow Test against a real host is walk-only.

the Timeline section's container (3a-v-a, EditorTimeline.swift): its header and rows, and it takes no input itself. What it draws is read by 3a-v-a-timeline.jsonl, 3a-v-a-timeline-rename.jsonl and 3a-v-a-timeline-more.jsonl; its controls are editor.timeline.toggle, .uncommitted, .row.<…> and .more, each pressed there.

not an identifier: the `@AppStorage("editor.timeline.open")` key that holds whether the Timeline is open (EditorTimeline.swift:25). The harvest reads every literal shaped like an identifier, so it counts a defaults key no element carries and no check can press. The open state it holds IS driven: 3a-v-a-timeline.jsonl presses editor.timeline.toggle closed and open again and asserts the rows go and come back.

a Text (3a-v-a, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses an Inline blame write the pane itself offers (On or Off), and Go refuses a boolean only when settings.json does not parse — which, as for settings.editor.showIgnored.refusal, no fixture or step can produce.
