the Timeline's Load more (3a-v-a): the last row of a LazyVStack inside a ScrollView capped at 240pt, so it is built only once the list is scrolled to its end — after a full page of 50 rows. Measured 2026-10-23 with 51 commits on log.txt: the accessibility tree held 15 of the 50 rows, and editor.timeline.more matched no element; no step kind scrolls. The page size and the end of history are pinned by WakilKitTests (editorTimelineHasMore: a full page has more, a short one is the end); pressing it is the runbook's row 5.

the Close Conversation prompt's container (.contain, conversations, Rule 1): the question and two buttons; it takes focus so Return and Escape keep. Read, not pressed — agent/conversations-close-asks.jsonl asserts its focus and its question; its buttons window.closeConversation.keep / .close are pressed there.

a Text (conversations, Rule 1): the prompt's question. Read, not pressed — agent/conversations-close-asks.jsonl asserts "Close this conversation? The agent is still working; what it is doing now stops." and its absence after Keep it.

its parity (Ticket view): the operator's channels are ⌥↓ / ⌥↑ — keys, from the Ticket column or from a review box inside the WKWebView — never a click on a control, so no parity step can drive a UI half (editor_peek_step's case). The dispatch is covered by ticket-review-step.jsonl (from none, from a thread, both directions, the column left on Ticket), which also steps once with ⌥↓ from the column.

its parity and a posted resolve (Ticket view, Decision 46): the operator's Resolve and Unresolve are buttons in a review box, HTML inside the WKWebView with no accessibility identifier (editor_peek's case); the agent's is priced gate, so a dispatch parks for the plane and holds its step open (editor_changes_branch_delete's case). What the agent meets before the plane is covered by ticket-agent-refusals.jsonl: a named PR that is not the thread's, and a thread GitHub does not know, each refused whole. A real resolve read back on GitHub is the walk's.

its parity and a posted reply (Ticket view): Send is a button in a review box, HTML inside the WKWebView with no accessibility identifier, and the action is priced gate on every channel, so an agent's dispatch parks for the plane and holds its step open (editor_changes_branch_delete's case). Its refusals before any plane — a repo or PR that is not where GitHub says the thread is, a thread GitHub does not know, a root outside the project — are covered by ticket-agent-refusals.jsonl. The plane's words and a real reply read back on GitHub are the walk's.

its parity (Ticket view): the operator's channel is typing in a review box's reply field, inside the WKWebView, which no arm can address. The dispatch is covered by ticket-reply-draft.jsonl: drafts kept per thread, dropped by null and by empty text, read_pane naming the thread and never the words.

its parity (Ticket view): both channels ask https://api.github.com/user with the stored token (wakilcore's gitUserAPI has no endpoint seam, unlike WAKIL_GITHUB_API), so a pressed Test or a successful dispatch is a real network call with a fixture token. Its refusals before any call — an SSH account without API access, a host with no account — are dispatched by ticket-api-access.jsonl, which never presses Test; a real test is the walk's.

its parity (Ticket view): the operator's writes are typing into a field and leaving it (Next, a line, + then the new line), never a click, and the one click that writes — a line's × — consumes its subject: the same remove dispatched after it is refused (`no line "n1" in notDone`, measured), db_remove_database's case. Both channels ARE covered: ticket-record-line.jsonl and ticket-next-kept.jsonl write as the operator (read back from disk with plutil), ticket-agent-line.jsonl as the agent (`agent`, `edited by agent`, two refusals).

the Ticket view's container (Ticket view): a ScrollView that takes the column's keyboard focus — AXFocused is refused on it (axresolve not_focusable, measured) — so it is read, not pressed: ticket-tab-focus.jsonl and ticket-review-step.jsonl assert focus on it after the Ticket tab's click, and every ticket-*.jsonl frame holds controls inside it.

a failing check's `details ↗` (Ticket view): a SwiftUI Link to the check on github.com, so pressing it opens the default browser on a real page — a real trip (settings.row.<…>.reauthenticate's case). Its row (`✗ lint`) and the PR line's `1 failing` are read by ticket-header.jsonl.
a Text (Ticket view, Rule 8): a root's read that failed with none landed, whole. Read, not pressed — ticket-not-a-repo.jsonl asserts `not a git repository` for the git project's plain root after ↻.

a Text (Ticket view, Rule 8): a re-read that failed after one landed, whole, the last read kept. Read, not pressed — ticket-read-failures.jsonl moves e2e-api's .git away, presses ↻, and asserts `not a git repository` with In flight still drawn.

the ticket header's container (Ticket view, .contain): key, title and status — the PM tool's fields only, in the Ticket section (walk 2026-10-29: who it waits on moved to Pull requests as editor.ticket.waiting). Read, not pressed — ticket-header.jsonl asserts `INI-142 Log in with a token In Progress` and, separately, `waiting on reviewer, you`; ticket-narrow.jsonl holds it inside the view and clear of ↻.

a Text (Ticket view): `Reading In flight…`, drawn only until In flight's first read lands, which the GitHub stub answers at once — the only way to prolong it is to stall the organisation-wide search that every default-branch check needs (category 5's case, for a read). The rows it gives way to are pressed by ticket-in-flight.jsonl.
a Text (Ticket view): `Reading the ticket…` before a root's first read lands. Read, not pressed — ticket-refresh-cancel.jsonl asserts it while the stalled branch reads.
a Text (Ticket view): where Wakil looked for a ticket. Read, not pressed — ticket-link-agent.jsonl asserts `Looked in the branch name`.
a Text (Ticket view): `No ticket found for <branch>`. Read, not pressed — ticket-link-agent.jsonl asserts it before the agent's link and after its unlink.

a Text (Ticket view, Rule 8): a source that could not be read, whole. Read, not pressed — ticket-header.jsonl asserts the Jira line, ticket-github-error.jsonl GitHub's error, ticket-api-access.jsonl the SSH account's `Add API access …` line.

a Text (Ticket view): a pull request's line. Read, not pressed — ticket-header.jsonl and ticket-in-flight.jsonl assert `#212  ini-142-login → main      open · checks 1/2 · 1 failing`; ticket-narrow.jsonl holds it on one line inside the view.
the busy tick beside Cancel (Ticket view): drawn while a read runs, no press action. Read by frame — ticket-refresh-cancel.jsonl holds it inside the view while the stalled branch reads.

the record's container (Ticket view, .contain): its label, count, lines and + Add. Read, not pressed — ticket-record-line.jsonl reads `1 decision` and `1 not done` in it and presses editor.ticket.add then editor.ticket.add:notDone; ticket-narrow.jsonl holds it inside the view.
a Text (Ticket view): which root the view follows, drawn with more than one root. Read by frame — ticket-narrow.jsonl holds it inside the view and clear of ↻.

a Text (Ticket view, Rule 8): a picked ticket's branch that could not be read, whole. Read, not pressed — ticket-read-failures.jsonl picks INI-180 after its root's .git is moved away and asserts `not a git repository`.

a Text (Ticket view): `Reading <branch>…` while a picked ticket's branch reads. Read, not pressed — ticket-in-flight.jsonl picks INI-160, whose branch the GitHub stub stalls, and asserts `Reading ini-160-stall…`.

a Text (Ticket view, Rule 8): a record write's refusal, whole. Read, not pressed — ticket-write-refused.jsonl makes the tickets folder read-only, leaves Next, and asserts `permission denied` with the typed text kept.

not an identifier: GitAPIAccessRowView's `id` property (GitAccountsSection.swift:693), the prefix its controls extend — `.detail`, `.token`, `.token.field`, `.token.store`, `.test`, `.remove`, `.remove.keep`, `.remove.confirm`. The harvest reads the literal as an identifier, and no element carries it. The row's controls are pressed by ticket-api-access.jsonl (all but `.test`, which asks api.github.com: see ctx_git_api_access_test).

column1: # ---- 6. Only the walk reaches it: the browser's page (3c-i) ------------------
# What a web page asks for that the fixture cannot make it ask: a certificate
# WebKit does not trust (the stub is plain loopback http), a web content
# process that crashes (WebKit gives no way to crash one on purpose), an HTTP
# sign-in, and a file revealed in Finder (its effect leaves the window). The
# Three walk-only flows have no Wakil surface for an entry to name, and an
# entry that excuses nothing fails the gate, so they are recorded here, as
# comments, with their reason and where the walk covers them:
#   - a page's file chooser (<input type=file>): WebKit asks Wakil for an open
#     panel and Wakil shows the system's NSOpenPanel, whose controls are AppKit's,
#     not Wakil's, and no step kind drives a system panel. Runbook §3.
#   - Web Inspector (Inspect Element): offered by WebKit's own context menu on
#     the page, and no arm opens a context menu (editor_rename's case); the
#     inspector is WebKit's window. Runbook row 9.
#   - a pop-up sign-in (GitHub OAuth): needs a real identity provider and a real
#     account, and a check signing in leaves a real credential behind (#254's
#     rule). The pop-up-as-a-tab mechanics are 3c-i-tabs.jsonl's popup.html.
# The final review's fixes add four more, each a relaunch or a place's new name
# — one check is one launch, and the seeded launch opens its first pane inside
# a conversation, so no page loads before a canvas is adopted:
#   - a page kept, not reloaded, when a conversation takes the canvas or the
#     project or environment is renamed (I1): WakilKit's
#     aRenamedProjectRehomesTheBrowser pin the call and the state files' move.
#   - a new tab never showing an earlier pane's page after a relaunch (I2):
#   - a tab's scroll and same-page moves kept across a quit (I8). Runbook row 4.
#   - a failed download's line shown whole (I5): the fixture's downloads do not
#     fail, and the accessibility text is whole whether or not it is cut on

column2: a Text (3c-i): `<host>'s certificate isn't trusted — <reason>`. Drawn only over an https page whose certificate WebKit refuses, and the page stub is loopback http; walk-only (runbook §3, self-signed.badssl.com).
Visit Anyway (3c-i, operator only, for the session): drawn only on the certificate page (browser.certificate's case); walk-only.
a Text (3c-i): `This page stopped.`. Drawn only after WebKit's web content process for the tab ends, and nothing a check can do crashes it; walk-only (runbook §3).
Reload on the crashed page (3c-i): browser.crashed's case; walk-only.
an HTTP sign-in's user name (3c-i): drawn only for a basic-auth challenge, which the page stub never sends; walk-only (runbook §3).
an HTTP sign-in's password (3c-i): browser.prompt.user's case — and a check typing a password is a credential in a check file; walk-only.

Show in Finder (3c-i): drawn only on a finished download, and pressing it reveals the file in Finder — the act's whole effect leaves the window (settings.org.git.account.add.openKeys' case). The fixture's big.bin takes minutes by design; a real download is the runbook's row 7.

the camera / microphone prompt's Allow (3c-i): drawn only when a page asks for a camera or microphone, and macOS first asks the operator itself (TCC), a system dialog no step kind answers; a fixture camera would also have to exist. Walk-only: runbook row 8.
the camera / microphone prompt's Don't Allow (3c-i): browser.prompt.allow's case. Walk-only: runbook row 8.

Open on a page's app link (3c-i, final review I4): pressing it hands the link to the app macOS names for it (Mail, Zoom) — the act's whole effect leaves the window (settings.org.git.account.add.openKeys' case). The question and its Cancel are 3c-i-app-link.jsonl's; Open is walk-only (runbook §3).

its dispatch and its parity (3c-i, final review I6): its whole effect is the system's print panel, a sheet of AppKit's controls that no step kind drives (a page's file chooser's case). The ⌘K row Print page is 3c-i-app-link.jsonl's; printing is runbook row 9.

column1: # What no check can show, each with its reason and where the walk covers it.
# None names a Wakil surface an entry could excuse (an entry that excuses
# nothing fails the gate), so each is recorded here as a comment:
#   - what a real site's page does with Wakil's page script: framework-controlled
#     fields (React and the like, which see the act only through real input
#     events), open shadow roots and cross-origin frames. The fixtures don't have
#     them: no fixture page uses a framework, a shadow root or a frame. Runbook
#   - an agent's click on a target=_blank link: the page opens a tab of its
#     own (a pop-up, BrowserTabHost.adoptPopup), which the act did not ask for
#     and which may come to the front as a page's pop-up does. No fixture form
#     links out that way, and whether the new tab takes the front is the
#     pop-up's behaviour, not the driver's (the driver selects no tab). Walk-only.
#   - a page that moves focus while the agent types (a focus trap, a step that
#     jumps to a password or code field): the script checks the focused
#     element, through open shadow roots, is still the target before the text
#     goes in, else refuses as a changed page and types nothing (final review
#     I2). No fixture page moves focus on its own; the refusal was proven once
#     in an offscreen WKWebView whose focus handlers jump to a password field.
#   - the 1 s idle wait: no arm types into the page while a scripted act waits
#     on it — a do step and the stub's call run one after the other, never
#     together — so the wait, and the refusal after 10 s of continuous input,
#     cannot be raised. The wait's arithmetic is WakilKit's browserIdleWait.
#   - colour: the site question's neutral edge (against the production plane's
#     red) and the amber untrusted row in the thread. No step kind reads a
#     colour; the words of both are 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl's and
#   - a spoken act made of the scripted sentence alone: every launch's speech
#     script settles on one fixed sentence (e2e/driver/speech.go), whose stub
#     covers the spoken site question by adding typed words to the landed
#     sentence (the turn stays spoken until the composer is emptied): the
#     type confirm field shows, Return without the word does nothing, and
#     Allow answers once confirm is typed (Invariant 7). Runbook row 6.
# The agent's acts in a page have no Wakil control as their operator's half, so their parity

column2: its parity (3c-ii): the operator's channel is the page itself — typing into a field in the web view, and WebKit does not carry a field's DOM id as its AXIdentifier, so no `do` step names it and a parity step has no UI half to drive. Measured 2026-10-26: a page giving <input id="browser.page.guest">, a `do.type` into browser.page.guest failed with axresolve not_found (matched no element). The agent's channel IS covered: 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl types the guest name through the scripted agent after Allow and asserts the page's title after Return ("Booked: Ada Lovelace, 2 nights"), refuses the card field (Invariant 6), and keeps the keyboard in the composer (Rule 6); 3c-ii-read-and-refusals.jsonl dispatches its refusals.

its parity (3c-ii): the operator's channel is the page itself — choosing an option in the page's own <select> in the web view, and WebKit does not carry a <select>'s DOM id as its AXIdentifier, so no `do` step names it and a parity step has no UI half to drive. Measured 2026-10-26: a page giving <select id="browser.page.nights">, a `do.focus` on browser.page.nights failed with axresolve not_found (matched no element). The agent's channel IS covered: 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl chooses Two nights through the scripted agent and asserts it in the booked title ("2 nights"); 3c-ii-read-and-refusals.jsonl dispatches its refusals.

its parity (3c-ii): the operator's channel is the page itself — a key pressed in a page field in the web view. A `do.press` sends its key to whatever holds the keyboard, so its UI half needs the page field focused first, and no step can focus one: measured 2026-10-26, a `do.type` into <input id="browser.page.guest"> and a `do.focus` on <select id="browser.page.nights"> each failed with axresolve not_found, WebKit not carrying a DOM id as the AXIdentifier. The agent's channel IS covered: 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl presses Return in the guest name through the scripted agent and asserts the submitted page's title; 3c-ii-read-and-refusals.jsonl dispatches its refusals.

its parity (3c-ii): the operator's channel is the page itself — a click on a page element in the web view, and WebKit does not carry an element's DOM id as its AXIdentifier, so no `do` step names it and a parity step has no UI half to drive. Measured 2026-10-26: form.html given <a id="browser.page.jump" href="#bottom">, a parity after Allow clicking browser.page.jump failed its UI half with axresolve not_found (matched no element); the dispatch half was never in question — after Allow the harness speaks as the allowed conversation, and 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl dispatches browser_scroll there without a park. The agent's channel IS covered: 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl clicks Confirm through the scripted agent and asserts the booked title, and 3c-ii-production.jsonl clicks it on a production site after the typed confirm; 3c-ii-read-and-refusals.jsonl dispatches its refusals.

its parity (3c-ii): the operator's channel is the page itself — scrolling the web view, a scroll wheel and not a click or a drag, so a parity step has no UI half to drive (browser_zoom's case); and where a page sits after a scroll is not in read_pane or the tree a parity compares. The agent's channel IS covered by 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl: the scripted agent scrolls to the back link (`scrolled to "Back to page A"`), and a dispatch after Allow scrolls again with the keyboard left in the composer.

its parity (3c-ii): the click consumes its own subject — the agent-allowed mark's × takes the site off and the mark goes, so a dispatch after it revokes nothing and the halves cannot read back a change (ctx_unlink_provider's case); and the mark is drawn only after the scripted agent was allowed, which a parity's dispatch half cannot raise again. The × channel IS covered by 3c-ii-act-allowed.jsonl: browser.agentAllowed.revoke twice, each followed by the mark gone. The dispatch is covered only as a no-op: one dispatch revokes example.com for another conversation and the mark stays; no check dispatches a revoke that takes effect, because the harness has no {conversation} token to name the screen's own.

the collapsed rail's 6 pt edge zone (rail collapse): it is a hover target — the pointer resting there 150 ms slides the rail out over the canvas, and 300 ms after the pointer leaves it goes — and no step kind hovers or rests a pointer, nor measures a delay or a slide (window.contextLine.branch's case). What it can be asked is covered: rail-collapse.jsonl asserts it is in the tree at the window's right edge no wider than 8 pt while collapsed, and the spine beside it by press. The hover peek, its two timings, the slide's travel and the plane's opacity-and-blur release (400–600 ms), the Reduce Motion crossfade and "peeking never takes focus" are the walk's (docs/wakil/rail-collapse-acceptance.md rows 2–5); the timings and the spine's marks are WakilKitTests': RailSpineTests.

its parity (names): the operator's channel is typing a name in ⌘K or ⌘P's name step (or a Running row's field) and pressing Return or leaving — typing and a leave, not one click or drag, ctx_rename_project's case. Both channels ARE covered: the name step by names-rename-palette.jsonl and names-rename-running-cmd-r.jsonl, the dispatch by names-rename-dispatch.jsonl and names-operator-wins.jsonl, each asserting the new name in the tree (the Landing's Running row, ⌘P's, the chip's label) and the old one gone; what no check can express is the comparison of the two channels' resulting state, which a parity step makes.

Copy (3d-iv) and its neighbour Reveal ask for LocalAuthentication first (LAContext .deviceOwnerAuthentication), the system's Touch ID / password sheet, outside the app's accessibility tree: no step can approve or cancel it, so a press could assert nothing but a sheet left over the run. Copy then puts the value on the SYSTEM PASTEBOARD, marked concealed, which no check can read (api.recent.<…>.curl's case). Reveal has no entry of its own only because the controls extractor does not list its identifier (its title and its identifier share a ternary line); the same reason applies to it. What the checks can reach is the list, Edit, Delete and Keep it, never-saved ×, and the refusals around them. The authentication, the reveal and the copy are the runbook's row 8 (docs/wakil/phase-3d-iv-acceptance.md).

Choose File… in the import sheet (3d-iv) opens the macOS file picker (NSOpenPanel), a system panel outside the app's accessibility tree that no step can choose a file in or cancel (settings.projects.add.folder's case). The import itself is covered through the sheet's own controls and browser_password_save; the picker is the runbook's row 9 (docs/wakil/phase-3d-iv-acceptance.md). Not an entry, because it is not surface: the Keychain's own prompt when another program (the agent's `security`) asks for a value, and the rebuilt app's first read, are the runbook's row 10, and no check can see a system dialog.

column1: # ---- 3d-i: tab groups, pins and the vertical column ---------------------------

column2: its parity (3d-i): the operator's channel is ⌃⌘S or the Browser menu's Toggle Tab Column — a key and a menu-bar item, not a click or a drag (browser_zoom's case). Both are covered by 3d-i-vertical-column.jsonl: ⌃⌘S hides and shows the column (tabColumnHidden read back, the edge's frame), and the dispatch hides one pane's column and leaves another's.

its parity (3d-i): the operator's channels are ⌘R on the pull-request group's header and its menu's Refresh, and that group exists only for an organisation whose GitHub account keeps a token — the fixture has no GitHub account, and a token would send the search to api.github.com. The dispatch is 3d-i-settings-tabs.jsonl's (absent: no group in the pane); runbook row 7 walks the group, ⌘R and the ↻.

a group's name field (3d-i): opened only by the group menu's Rename… and the tab menu's New Group… — no step kind double-clicks or opens a context menu. Rule 2 (focus leaving keeps the name), Rule 3 (it arrives focused, the name selected) and Rule 7 (an empty name is ignored) are walk-only for it; runbook row 3. The rename itself is 3d-i-own-groups.jsonl's dispatch.

the pull-request group's ↻ (3d-i, Rule 5): an image with no press action, drawn only while a pull-request refresh runs on a pane holding the group — which needs a GitHub account with a token (browser_pull_requests_refresh's case). Runbook row 7.

a Text (3d-i, Rule 8): the pull-request group's last refresh failure, under the strip. Drawn only when a refresh with a kept token fails, and the fixture has no GitHub account (browser_pull_requests_refresh's case). Walk-only: runbook row 7.

a Text (3d-i, Rule 8): why pins/<project>.json can't be read, under the strip. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-pins-unreadable.jsonl breaks the file from a terminal and holds browser.pinsError inside browser.pane, the pinsError non-null.

a Text (3d-i): `Press ⌘W again to close` under a pinned tab after a first ⌘W. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-pinned-close.jsonl holds browser.tab.t1.closeTip and browser.tab.t2.closeTip inside browser.pane and asserts the words come and go.
a Text (3d-i walk): `Copied`, under the address field for about 1.5 s after ⌘⇧C. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-copy-url.jsonl holds it inside browser.pane and asserts the word comes and goes.

the vertical tab column's container (.contain, 3d-i): its rows and ＋ are pressed as browser.tab.<id>, browser.group.<id> and browser.newTab. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-vertical-column.jsonl holds it inside browser.pane at 215–235 pt, clear of browser.page, at the narrow window too.

the hidden column's 6 pt edge (3d-i): a zone that peeks the column after the pointer rests on it 150 ms, with no press action — and no step kind moves the pointer without clicking. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-vertical-column.jsonl holds it inside browser.pane, at most 12 pt wide, once ⌃⌘S hides the column. The peek is walk-only: runbook row 8.

not an identifier: the coordinate space the column's drag measures its rows in (`.coordinateSpace(name:)`, BrowserTabColumn.swift:91). The harvest reads every literal shaped like an identifier, so it counts a name no element carries (editor.timeline.open's case).

not an identifier: the `@AppStorage("browser.tabColumn.width")` key that holds the column's app-wide width (BrowserTabColumn.swift:42) — editor.timeline.open's case. The width is dragged on the column's divider, which is hidden from accessibility, so the 160–360 clamp is walk-only (runbook row 8) and BrowserTabColumnRules' unit test.

the vertical column's pinned section (.contain, 3d-i walk): the tiles' grid and the pinned groups' rows, pressed as browser.tab.<id> and browser.group.<id>. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-pinned-section.jsonl holds it inside browser.tabColumn, a tile inside it at 40–56 pt both ways, and the unpinned tabs clear of it. That it is gone with nothing pinned has no tree assertion (an absent identifier is not a step kind, and its label is an AXDescription the tree text never prints): BrowserPinnedSectionTests' withNothingPinnedThereIsNoSection holds it, and runbook row 18.

the pinned section's 0.5 pt line in the column (3d-i walk): a rule with no press action. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-pinned-section.jsonl holds it inside browser.tabColumn; its drop halves are BrowserPinnedSectionTests' theBandsHalvesAreEitherSideOfTheLine, and dragging across it in the column is runbook row 18.

the strip's line after the pinned tabs and groups (3d-i walk): a rule with no press action. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-pinned-section.jsonl holds it inside browser.tabs and drags a tab across it both ways (the browser_pin and browser_unpin parities).

the Tabs row's container (.contain, 3d-i): its choices are pressed as settings.browser.tabs.vertical and .horizontal by 3d-i-settings-tabs.jsonl and 3d-i-vertical-column.jsonl. Read, not pressed — held around its Vertical choice at the narrow window.

a Text (3d-i, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses a Tabs choice the pane itself offers (Horizontal or Vertical), which it does only when settings.json does not parse (settings.editor.inlineBlame.refusal's case). 3d-i-settings-tabs.jsonl asserts the refusal of any other value through the dispatch.

the Name groups with AI row's container (.contain, 3d-i): its choices are pressed as settings.browser.nameGroups.on and .off by 3d-i-settings-tabs.jsonl. Read, not pressed — held around its Off choice at the narrow window.
a Text (3d-i, Rule 8): settings.browser.tabs.refusal's case — drawn only when Go refuses On or Off, which needs a settings.json that does not parse.

a Text (3d-i): why the organisation has no pull-request group, under Tabs. Read, not pressed — 3d-i-settings-tabs.jsonl asserts `No pull-request group: e2e-fixture has no GitHub account.` and holds it inside settings.pane at the narrow window.

a tab's in-place name field (names, 3d-i): drawn only after the tab menu's Rename Tab… in the strip or the column, a context menu no arm opens (editor_rename's case). Its commit is browser_rename_tab, dispatched by names-tab-rename.jsonl and run from ⌘K by the same check; the focus, selection, Return, leaving and Esc are walk-only.

the pencil after a renamed tab's name (names, 3d-i): an Image, read not pressed — names-tab-rename.jsonl and names-tab-rename-column.jsonl hold it inside browser.tabs and browser.tabColumn, at the narrow window too.

its parity (names, 3d-i): the operator's channel is typing a name in ⌘K's name step or the tab's in-place field and pressing Return or leaving — typing and a leave, not one click or drag (ctx_rename_project's case).
